name: Verifier-guided search inference for code (pass@16 quality at pass@4 cost)
one_line: A Morph-style specialized provider for coding agents: send a prompt plus tests, an in-engine verify-abort-refill scheduler returns the first passing sample; measured 2.63x fewer decode tokens and 2.12x faster at identical pass@16 on HumanEval with an 8B model, with the repo's own 'buyer-replicable' verdict confronted via pre-registered gates.

numeric_claims.claim: Continuous scheduler pass@16 0.884 vs naive 0.884 (identical)
327,607 vs 862,050 decode tokens = 2.63x fewer
86.6 s vs 183.8 s end-to-end wall = 2.12x faster
Round engine: 330,174 tokens (2.60x), 110.0 vs 168.1 s GPU generation wall (1.53x), pass 0.878 vs 0.896, verify 18.6 vs 27.0 s
Post-hoc pass@16 0.909; naive 860,830 tokens
Setup: 164 HumanEval problems, N=16, B=4, temperature 0.8, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 640, seed 0, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, A100-80GB, vLLM 0.24.0, max_model_len 4096, enforce_eager
Verifier = check() in a subprocess with 10 s timeout
Naive baseline ran second on a warm prefix cache (bias against scheduler)
modal_verifier_sched.py is 194 lines
Weak verifier Llama-3.1-8B: oracle 0.909, weak 0.848 (93%), visible FP 7.7%, oracle cost 2.85x, weak cost 3.04x
Weak verifier Qwen2.5-Coder-7B: oracle 0.963, weak 0.921 (96%), FP 3.8%, oracle cost 3.45x, weak cost 3.52x

HumanEval pass 0.689 -> 0.829 -> 0.902 at N=1/4/16; tokens 52k -> 858k; TriviaQA 0.680 -> 0.693
Best-of-N costs ~16x tokens naively

Agentic-value v1: 1.4x/5.0x/11.5x vs re-prefill, 1.00x/1.01x/1.02x vs cached, 2x/4x/4x fewer decode tokens at W/B 4k/4, 16k/8, 32k/8

founder_decisions.decision: Delivery form: hosted API vs open-source scheduler vs SDK vs all three
founder_decisions.options: Hosted /v1/solve endpoint; Apache-2.0 scheduler plugin for vLLM/SGLang; client SDK implementing round-based early stop on any provider; a combination
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The ledger says the token saving is buyer-replicable; whether the in-engine increment (bounded 1.53x -> 2.12x across two runs) justifies a hosted engine is the section 10 row-6 gate plus a business-model judgment. Morph/Relace are hosted and closed; LMCache/Tensormesh is OSS plus hosted (05-research-kvcache.md).

founder_decisions.options: Treat as validation of the buyer and distribution pattern; treat as a reason to pick a different beachhead; treat as a partnership/acquirer path
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Facts only: none ships a verifier endpoint in the research files; all sell to the same buyer; Morph's published SWE-Bench Pro lifts are +2.1 to +3.7 points. The founder's rule forbids an 'already exists' judgment here.

founder_decisions.options: 7-8B (Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, measured); 30B-A3B class (OpenHands default, unmeasured); frontier open MoE (Kimi K2.7 Code, GLM-5.2, unmeasured); a fine-tuned code model with a custom speculator (Relace/Morph recipe)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Only 7-8B is measured; the Unproven row-2 experiment informs it, and the choice sets GPU cost, ceiling pass rate, and which buyers can use the endpoint.

founder_decisions.options: A100 (measured); H100/H200; B200; AMD MI355X (Wafer's numbers)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Nothing is measured off A100-80GB; unit economics (Unproven row 7) depend on the rental rate and per-solve GPU-seconds that must be measured on the chosen class.

founder_decisions.options: vLLM 0.24 LLMEngine (measured scheduler); SGLang (measured under load and at long prefixes); a fork of either with the scheduler in-tree
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: vLLM's n>1 pathology at long prefixes (174x) vs SGLang's 2.2x is measured, but the product's independent-request branching at 100K+ is not (Unproven row 3); forking trades maintenance burden for control.

founder_decisions.options: Customer-supplied tests only; add a learned verifier/classifier in the style of Morph Reflexes; add static checks (lint/type) as cheap pre-verifiers
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The repos contain no evidence for learned verifiers; the measured 93-96% ceiling retention is for test-based verifiers only.

founder_decisions.options: Per solve with a token budget; per token at peer list rates; reserved GPU-hours with scheduler included; savings-share (Tensormesh's 30%-of-savings precedent)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Per-solve GPU-seconds at production concurrency are unmeasured; the architecture makes token bills fall, so the unit determines whether the provider's revenue and the buyer's saving point the same way.

founder_decisions.decision: Market size and the generation-vs-search share of coding-agent spend
founder_decisions.options: Judge the beachhead large enough; judge it too narrow; defer until pilot data
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Explicitly excluded by the founder's rule; the files give search at 56.6% of coding-trace tokens (Relace) and Anthropic's ~400k sessions with ~4 user turns and ~10 actions per prompt, but no spend figures.

founder_decisions.decision: How to read the ledger's 'buyer-replicable, not a moat' verdict
founder_decisions.options: Disqualifying for a hosted engine; a statement about where to place the gate (section 10 row 6); irrelevant if distribution and per-solve pricing are the product
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The repo itself left this unreconciled (04-conflicts.md conflict 6) and moved to a different thesis without amending it; it is a judgment about defensibility, not a measurement.
